request_text: Break prd.md down into a backlog.
agent_reply:
The backlog is ready for review: `backlog_validate` reports `ready_for_review: true` with no blocking issues.

- **Files:** `/outputs/clinic-test-2/backlog/backlog.json` and `/outputs/clinic-test-2/backlog/backlog.md`.
- **Size:** 9 epics, 83 stories, 648 tasks and 381 story points. Every estimate is `llm` with low confidence, because there is no history file (`phase4/history.json`) to estimate from.
- **Epics:**
  - E-001 platform foundation and delivery
  - E-002 sign-in, roles and staff accounts
  - E-003 clinics, hours, leave, treatments and free slots
  - E-004 online booking
  - E-005 manage appointments
  - E-006 reception and dentist day
  - E-007 messaging and reminders
  - E-008 family members (Release 2)
  - E-009 no-show block and report (Release 2)
- **Coverage:** every FR and NFR in the PRD maps to at least one story.
- **Dependencies:** I added 26 cross-epic story dependencies, each with confidence 0.7 or higher.
- **Spec-kit fixes:** `backlog_build` first failed on stray `- [P] …` note lines at the end of six `tasks.md` files, so I reworded those lines.

Open questions are carried on 17 stories; the validator lists these as its only warning. They fall into three groups:
- **Client confirmation needed:**
  - hosting and domain (Q-008)
  - the WhatsApp-to-SMS fallback
  - whether families need separate sign-ins (Q-007)
  - whether edit and remove of family members are out of Release 2
  - whether template wording can carry a family member's name
  - the performance and availability targets
- **Assumed defaults:**
  - staff password reset is done by the manager
  - alert recipients are a shared team channel
  - the sign-in code throttle values (10 per IP per hour, 5 per phone per hour, 1,000 codes a day)
- **Team decisions:**
  - Erasure on request (S-002-US6) was raised to must/P1 even though NFR-007 is not in the DL-1 requirement list.
  - Several stories were raised to must/P1 because their requirements fall in the Release 1 deadline: E-004's concurrency-proof story, and E-006's two stories on reception reschedule/cancel and the dentist's day.
  - E-007's foundational story is 13 points, the maximum. It can be split along its checkpoints.

File paths in the spec-kit tasks are guesses at the repo layout, since the real structure isn't known yet. `backlog_validate` did not flag them.

verdict.summary: backlog_check reports no blocking issues (9 epics, 83 stories, 648 tasks, 381 SP). The coverage map has a story for every prd.md requirement, FR-001 to FR-033 and NFR-001 to NFR-011. Release 2 items (FR-006, FR-025, FR-026, FR-029, FR-032, FR-033) are kept as P2/should. The sampled stories have measurable acceptance criteria. Auth, migration, infrastructure and secrets tasks are `ai_eligible` false. Priority raises, the unconfirmed hosting provider and domain, the SMS fallback, Q-007 and the unchosen providers appear in the Open questions section. Warnings a human can accept: (1) The per-feature specs disagree on file layout, so the backlog is inconsistent across epics. Feature 001 uses `clinic-api/src/clinic_api/...`, features 002 and 007 to 009 use `clinic-api/app/...` (and `app/modules/...`), and migrations live in `alembic/versions` for most features but `migrations/versions` for 009 and 001's env.py. (2) Feature flags are specified twice: 001-T094 to T101 build a DB-backed `GET /api/v1/feature-flags`, and 008-T001 and T007 add a separate settings-based `GET /api/feature-flags`. Reconcile this before sprint planning, for example by making 008 reuse 001's mechanism. (3) The SETUP, FOUND and POLISH pseudo-stories have only a generic 'meets Definition of Done' criterion. (4) Several priorities were raised above the spec's value and are flagged for PM confirmation.
